Purge the CDN Cache after Changing Clincoo CSS

Old CSS at the CDN edge makes a new release look broken. Purge or rename the file after every style deploy.

This article is available in: Indonesia · English

You already deployed new HTML, but visitors still see buttons with the old radius. That is not a CSS bug. style.css is still cached at the CDN with a long max-age.

Two safe paths: rename the file (a hash in the name, such as style.3f2a.css) and link it from HTML, or purge the CSS URL in the CDN dashboard right after release. Do not rely on visitors doing a hard refresh.

If you use Pages or Clincoo static hosting, check the Cache-Control header in the Network tab. Assets marked immutable must change URL. HTML can stay short-lived so the new CSS link arrives quickly.

After a purge, open the site in a private window without Disable cache. If styles are still old, a service worker may hold a copy. Remove the old worker, then test again.

Make purge the last step on the deploy checklist, equal to checking links and forms. A release that is "live" but still wearing yesterday's CSS breaks client trust.
